Calculate the integral ∫(log3⁡x)2dx.

a
x((log3⁡x)2+2log3⁡(x)ln⁡3−2ln2⁡3)+C
b
2x((log3⁡x)2−log3⁡(x)ln⁡3−1ln2⁡3)+C
c
x((log3⁡x)2−3log3⁡(x)ln⁡3+3ln2⁡3)+C
d
x((log3⁡x)2−2log3⁡(x)ln⁡3+2ln2⁡3)+C
e
2x(3(log3⁡x)2+log3⁡(x)ln⁡3+2ln2⁡3)+C

decision.explanation: Since log₃(x)=ln(x)/ln(3), integration by parts twice gives ∫(ln x)² dx=x((ln x)²−2ln x+2)+C. Dividing by (ln 3)² yields option d.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}(x)-\int (x)(\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int {log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate  $\int {log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{3}⁡(x))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =x{({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(x{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D) \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2x{log}_{3}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{2x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}-\frac{2D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =x({({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{2}{{ln}^{2}⁡3})+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{2D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}(x)-\int (x)(\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int {log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate  $\int {log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{3}⁡(x))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =x{({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(x{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D) \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2x{log}_{3}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{2x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}-\frac{2D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =x({({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{2}{{ln}^{2}⁡3})+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{2D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

We need to use integration by parts. 

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(2{x}^{2})(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})(4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+2\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts twice gives the antiderivative x⁵[5(ln x)²−2ln x+2/5]. At x=e this is 17e⁵/5, and at x=1 it is 2/5. Their difference is (17e⁵−2)/5, option c.

after.worked_solution:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2} & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=25{x}^{4} & \,⟹\,v=\int 25{x}^{4}\text{d}x=5{x}^{5}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 25{x}^{4}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & ={(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}(5{x}^{5})-\int (5{x}^{5})(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x})\text{d}x \\  & =5{x}^{5}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-10\int {x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int {x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={x}^{4} & \,⟹\,v=\int {x}^{4}\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(\frac{{x}^{5}}{5})-\int (\frac{{x}^{5}}{5})(\frac{1}{x})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\int {x}^{4}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{5}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{25}+D\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 25{x}^{4}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\text{d}x & =5{x}^{5}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-10\int {x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\text{d}x \\  & =5{x}^{5}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-10(\frac{{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{5}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{25}+D) \\  & =5{x}^{5}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-2{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\frac{2{x}^{5}}{5}-10D \\  & ={x}^{5}(5{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\frac{2}{5})+C\,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-10D.$ Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}25{x}^{4}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\text{d}x & ={[{x}^{5}(5{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\frac{2}{5})]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =[{e}^{5}(5{(\operatorname{ln}⁡e)}^{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡e+\frac{2}{5})]-[{1}^{5}(5{(\operatorname{ln}⁡1)}^{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡1+\frac{2}{5})] \\  & =[{e}^{5}(5-2+\frac{2}{5})]-\frac{2}{5} \\  & =\frac{17{e}^{5}-2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
